$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Row cooldown_time: <=900 s is for ordinary transients. Values over 900 s, up to the 86400 s cap, are reserved for rows with a named, self-refilling wall (a daily or monthly quota that outlasts 900 s) - the row stays live, parked, and re-probes itself; each such row cites its issue in a comment (fleet-ops#8398/#9075). A row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 must set model_info.allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0, because its 429s are OpenRouter's named daily free-tier wall and the row has to park on the first one (fleet-ops#9248). A row on api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4, api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1, token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 or api.minimax.io/anthropic must park the same way on its first 429 with a 6 h cooldown, because those 429s are a weekly quota, a drained prepaid balance, a monthly token cap or a spent token plan with fixed reset clocks, not bursts (fleet-ops#11146, #11234, #11417). A row on api.synthetic.new/openai/v1 must park on its first 429 (RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0) with the 900 s burst cool: its shared key answers both the 5-hour subscription pool's wall and the provider's own 'Too many concurrent requests' burst 429, LiteLLM v1.105.0 splits cooldown thresholds and lengths per exception class only so no config can tell the two kinds apart by text, and the short park keeps the burst trade bounded while the row re-probes itself (fleet-ops#11476, note 17 in docs/litellm-router-notes.md). Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. Every model_list row must declare its cache capability: model_info.supports_prompt_caching (boolean) and model_info.cache_proof (non-empty string, date plus measured cached tokens or a doc link), because ~0% cache-read on four provider groups was 70% of uncached router tokens and no rule forced a new seat to say which case it is (fleet-ops#9365). A worker-group row whose supports_prompt_caching is false must set litellm_params.order: 2 so long sessions fall to it only as overflow (order filtering is applied after the cooldown filter in LiteLLM v1.98.0 router.py, proven by tests/test_router_order2_overflow.py). router_settings.redis_host, redis_port and redis_password (os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD) are required and redis_url is forbidden (v1.98.0 drops the password when redis_url is set; the cache has requirepass): session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings. router_settings.allowed_fails_policy.NotFoundErrorAllowedFails must be 0 (fleet-ops#9469): a 404 is a withdrawn free model or a dead model id, and the per-exception threshold falls back to the router-level allowed_fails (1) for a key the policy does not name, so without it a dead lane needs two 404s to park and leaks one to the next caller. See the allowed_fails_policy property for the mechanism and for what the 404 cooldown costs on the quota-walled rows.

then.$comment: A tether row without its fallback would leave Tether unanswered on any Claude failure (Nish 2026-10-22: any Claude failure falls through to assistant).

tetherRow.$comment: Tether's Claude Sonnet 5.5 row (Nish 2026-10-22, fleet-ops#9980; 2026-10-23, Nishfleet/tether#7). The group, the model and the key are pinned together: the tether group answers only from claude-sonnet-5-5 on the Anthropic key, and that key serves no other group, so no routing group or fallback other than tether reaches the prepaid credit. The row carries a 50 USD/day wall (Nish 2026-10-23), and raising it is a deliberate change with its own issue. A caller holding the proxy master key can still name the group, so Tether's own virtual key is the only key that should list it.

retryPolicy.$comment: fleet-ops#9375: in-router retries must not re-send a worker prompt to a different seat more than the fallback needs. The values are locked by tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py: shipped (2,2,2) produced a third in-group pick that re-sent the whole prompt cold; the #9375 cut caps the worker group before the fallback group (or Pi's own retry, which keeps the session id and therefore the pin). On litellm 1.98.0 the one allowed retry goes back to the row that just failed when that row is still healthy after the 429 (router allowed_fails 1; the test drills it). A row that parks on its first 429 (RateLimitErrorAllowedFails 0, the daily-quota rows) is already cooling, so its retry goes to a peer: still capped at one extra pick, not a same-row retry. Either way the cap removes the third-seat re-send. A litellm upgrade can change that, which is why the test pins the version. ContentPolicyViolationErrorRetries is 0 because a content-policy refusal repeats on every seat; AuthenticationErrorRetries is 1 (fleet-ops#10756) because a 401 does not recover on the same row but the router-level AuthenticationErrorAllowedFails 0 (config/litellm-proxy.yaml router_settings.allowed_fails_policy, gated by test_the_live_config_parks_a_401_row_on_its_first_failure) parks the 401 row on its first failure, so the granted retry goes to a live peer in the same group and one dead provider key does not fail the whole session. TimeoutErrorRetries/InternalServerErrorRetries/BadRequestErrorRetries are capped at 1 (InternalServerErrorRetries is inert on 1.98.0: get_num_retries_from_retry_policy has no InternalServerError branch, so it was a forward bound only, and it went live with the v1.105.0 image move (fleet-ops#10071). fleet-ops#9050 adds NotFoundErrorRetries and DefaultRetries, both live on 1.105.0: the policy is read before should_retry_this_error, NotFoundErrorRetries covers a status-404 answer, and DefaultRetries covers every class the policy does not name (a 402 maps to APIError with no named key; a 403 from an openai-compatible provider arrives as BadRequestError carrying status 403, which BadRequestErrorRetries already granted on both 1.98.0 and 1.105.0). Whether the granted retry reaches a different row depends on rotation: a 404 parks the row on NotFoundErrorAllowedFails 0, so the retry went to a live peer; a 403 cools nothing, so the session pin overrides the skip list and the granted attempt re-picks the same row (both drilled on 1.105.0 in tests/test_router_retry_policy_no_cross_seat.py). Both are capped at 1 like the other retry keys; named keys keep precedence, so content-policy stays 0 and a 429 gets the second, peer-row retry. RateLimitErrorRetries is 2 (fleet-ops#10178: the second retry runs after the pinned row is parked and lands on a peer, so a one-slot row that is full does not leak a 429 from a group with no fallback). All keys are required and unknown keys are forbidden on purpose: a new litellm knob must arrive as a reviewed schema change, not a silent config edit.

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#10608 (Nish 2026-10-28): GLM-5.3-Flash is a worker model only and Qwen is a judge or reviewer only. A GLM-5.3-Flash row in any group but a worker group, or a Qwen row in a worker group, fails here. pilot is the gh-aw pilot's worker group (fleet-ops#11311).

Tether's Claude row: every row named tether is the pinned row, every row on the Anthropic key is a tether row, and there is at most one of each, so a second tether row, a tether row on another model or provider, or the Anthropic key on another group all fail here. Absence is allowed (the schema's own reject cases are built without it); router_settings.fallbacks requires tether -> assistant whenever the row exists.

fleet-ops#9365: a worker-group row proven unable to cache (supports_prompt_caching false) must sit at order 2, so long-session traffic stays on cache-capable rows and the false row serves only as overflow when order-1 rows are in cooldown.

Every worker row carries an integer weight >= 1 (Nish 2026-10-13 asked for more traffic on the unlimited ds41flash rows). LiteLLM v1.98.0 simple_shuffle.py:43-46 turns weighted picking on only when the FIRST healthy row of the group has a weight, and reads a missing weight as 0: one worker row without it either switches the weighting off or gives that row a 0 share (a bench the header forbids). A weight of 0 or below is the same bench, so the floor is 1.

fleet-ops#11146: a row on api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4, api.stepfun.ai/step_plan/v1, token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 or api.minimax.io/anthropic sits on a quota wall with a fixed reset clock, not a burst: the z.ai Coding Plan answers 429 code 1310 'Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted' naming its reset time, the Step Plan answers 429 'you have no left credit' while the prepaid balance is drained, the Alibaba token plan answers 429 'Your token-plan 1-month quota has been exhausted' naming its reset date, and the MiniMax token plan answers 429 'Token Plan usage limit reached (2056)' while the plan is spent: with the MINIMAX_API_KEY rows riding the burst treatment their plan re-enterings landed 179 of those 429s inside the #11417 alert window on 2026-10-31 (fleet-ops#11417). The 900 s burst cool with allowed_fails 1 re-enters the wall every 15 min and leaks it to the caller: 58.9% of worker-capable chat calls failed at 2026-10-30 02:28Z with 19 of the 29 worker-capable rows walled, and on 2026-10-31 the judge group held the RouterGroupJammed alert on the token-plan row alone, 107 of its 'quota has been exhausted' 429s in the journal from 20:00Z. The row parks on its first 429 for 6 h and re-probes about 4x/day, so a reset is picked up within hours (the #9075/#9122 treatment). No MiniMax api_base row carries max_parallel_requests (the rule below, #11417): with the row's 6 h park in force, the router's own concurrency 429 (notes 9 and 17: it is raised before any provider call, it counts into the cooldown, and a row's own cooldown_time names the park length per class) would park a healthy plan row 6 h on one slot spike, and the v1.105.0 slot leak (fleet-ops#10762) fills the slots of a freed-never stream; the plan's own 429s hold the key instead (the #10694 treatment).

model_info.$comment: fleet-ops#9365: cache_proof is checked for presence and non-emptiness only, so the gate catches a missing verdict but does not read the text - 'unknown' would pass. That is deliberate: a pattern demanding a date and a token count would reject the legitimate 'cannot cache, here is the vendor doc' proof. What holds a hollow claim down is the proof line being a real measurement a reviewer can re-derive, and the probe behind it being quoted on the PR.

allowed_fails_policy.$comment: fleet-ops#9469 (PR 9472 coordinator risk): a row-level allowed_fails_policy resolves per exception type BEFORE the router policy (Router.get_allowed_fails_from_policy), so a row naming NotFoundErrorAllowedFails: 1 needs two 404s to park and re-opens the leak the router-level 0 closes. If a row names the key at all, it must be 0.

fleet-ops#9469: a 404 is a withdrawn free model or a model id that no longer exists, and it must park the row on the FIRST one. LiteLLM v1.98.0 resolves the threshold per exception type (Router.get_allowed_fails_from_policy), and a key the policy does not name falls back to the router-level allowed_fails (1) - two 404s - so a dead lane is picked again and leaks the 404 to the next caller. NotFoundErrorAllowedFails is required and pinned to 0 for that reason. The other four keys are the ones this file already sets; additionalProperties is false so a typo (NotFoundErrorAllowedFail, NotFoundErrorFails) is a rejected config rather than a silent fallback to 1. When LiteLLM adds an exception type, add its key here too - a rejection naming an unknown key is expected friction, not a bug. A row's own cooldown_time is what the 404 cooldown lasts: 21600 s on the rows parked for a named quota wall, 900 s elsewhere - the rules above pin each family, so see config/litellm-proxy.yaml.

model_group_alias.$comment: fleet-ops#9330 desk arm of the 3-day token trial, and nothing else: an alias renames a group Pi already picks, so Pi's compaction.modelOverrides (keyed provider/model) can shorten that arm's context without moving a single call to another seat. Only a worker group a Pi job can pick has one, which is why worker-public is here and assistant is not. Pinned as a closed map because an alias also renames the fallback chain: Router._get_model_from_alias resolves the name before routing, but fallback_lookup_groups keys on the requested name, so an alias with no fallbacks entry of its own inherits nothing and a failed row ends the call (the 'No fallback model group' shape of fleet-ops#9290). tests/test_workflow_caps.py asserts each pair here is real, that no alias name shadows a model_name, and that the desk name agent.yml builds is listed.

fallbacks.$comment: Tether: the tether entry is exactly [assistant] (a Claude failure falls to the group Hermes already uses, never to a worker group or back), and no other group may fall into tether, so the Claude credit is spent by Tether alone. W10c: worker-capable is the strong group and never falls down, so no worker-capable entry may name worker-cheap, worker-public or assistant; a strong call with no healthy row fails at the caller.

optional_pre_call_checks.description: Must contain session_affinity. Without that pre-call check the router never runs DeploymentAffinityCheck, so a session pin cannot exist, every call in a session shuffles across vendors and the prompt cache never hits (fleet-ops#9361).
